transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, I'm here because I've been having this issue after work. I'm a cashier, and lately after my shifts, I just keep buying these huge takeout orders. 

Like, I'm talking enough burgers, fries, chicken, and desserts to feed an entire family. And I'll just... I'll sit there and eat almost all of it by myself before I even go home. It's gotten really out of hand, and I just need some help figuring it out.

After you finish eating these large amounts of food, do you ever feel the need to do something to 'undo' what you've eaten, such as making yourself throw up, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of that. I don't make myself throw up or take laxatives or anything like that. And I definitely don't exercise. I usually just... I just go home feeling really full and awful about what I just did. But I don't try to get rid of the food or undo it.

latest_inference.note: The patient explicitly denies compensatory behaviors (purging, excessive exercise), which effectively rules out Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2). Given the lack of compensatory behaviors and the description of binge episodes, the diagnosis narrows to Binge Eating Disorder.
